title: Aspiring writer-director here. I’ve got a question.

commenti.body: Why would classical poems written by someone in the past reveal a “life-shattering” truth about her life? Aren’t poems filled with themes and platitudes that apply in a more general sense, rather than personal? Unless she’s schizophrenic

Well, it’s a collective sequence of poems that forms its own distinct meaning when put altogether in a very specific manner. She’s not interpreting the poems simply on their own, but rather as part of the anthology they form. I should make that clearer in the description — thank you for making me realize that.

I feel like it could be done well enough. I think you're being a little too quick to dismiss the potential of like thousands of classic poems. I will say I'm not a huge fan of the name of the movie thougu.

The title seems a big vague and generic yet the synopsis is anything but that.

This seems like it’s more of an art film, you’re not putting butts in seats the way a blockbuster would and you’re not an established name like Nolan or even a Yorgos Lanthimos so the title should sell the concept.

That said, if you can get this made the title will change a dozen times before release so the people you’re selling to are less the potential audience and more potential producers and studios. So I’d think of the title like a one line elevator pitch

Some suggestions:

A Life Through Poetry

The Truth of Interpretation

Stiches of Prose

A Life Lived Through the Classics of Poetry

I might be totally off here but the story should shine through the title because the hardest part of writing a script is getting script readers to *read it* and a title that intrigues about the story itself gets them to the opening scene and the opening scene is the next hardest part.

You have some good name suggestions. I'm curious of the way this plot is going to be portrayed. Is it like a mystery? More of a horror of discovering trauma? Intense or more contemplative? I feel like that would help a lot in choosing the right title. If OP answered that I'm sure people could be a lot more helpful.
